entities.name: Nag Hammadi Library
entities.label: Evidence
entities.summary: A collection of 13 Coptic leather-bound papyrus codices discovered in 1945 near Nag Hammadi, Egypt, dating to the 4th century CE. Including the Gospel of Thomas, the Gospel of Philip, and other Gnostic texts, this library revolutionized understanding of early Christian diversity by revealing theological traditions suppressed by orthodox Christianity.
